Undergraduate Honours Thesis

Twisting Theory of Lie Algebras

September 2026–Present Supervisor: Dr. Curtis Wendlandt University of Saskatchewan

A developing study of twisting theory for Lie algebras and coalgebras, with a (co)homological perspective and possible extensions to Lie bialgebras.

Overview

This project builds on my work done during my first summer research under the supervision of Dr. Curtis Wendlandt. My first goal is to cover twisting theory of Lie algebras and coalgebras with some perspective from (co)homology. I then hope to cover the twisting theory of Lie bialgebras, and potentially further. I also hope to add some coverage of interpretation and applications of these theories.

Current scope

  • twisting theory of Lie algebras;
  • twisting theory of Lie coalgebras;
  • a perspective from Lie algebra and coalgebra (co)homology;
  • possible extension to Lie bialgebras;
  • interpretation and applications where appropriate.

Mathematical notation

Project pages and notes support LaTeX-style mathematics through MathJax. For example, inline notation such as $\mathfrak{g}$ and displayed equations such as

\[[x,y] = -[y,x]\]

can be written directly in Markdown.
